payload.goal:
Add order priority and backorders to this warehouse codebase, across every layer that already exists.

Domain  - src/domain/orders.ts:
- Export type OrderPriority = "standard" | "express".
- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.

Preserve all existing behaviour and keep every existing test passing. Put new tests next to the code they cover, inside the directories the test script already scans.

root.title: Add order priority and backorders
root.objective: Add priority-aware orders and backorder handling across the warehouse stack without regressing existing behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Orders accept optional priority and default to standard when omitted.
Backorders are recorded and exposed instead of being treated as a hard reservation failure.
Priority-sensitive layers observe the new contract without breaking existing callers.
The new probe script is deterministic and integrated into the manifest.
Existing tests remain green after the change

children.title: Extend the order domain
children.objective: Add priority defaults, backorder records, and backorder listing to the order domain.
expectedOutcomes: `OrderPriority` is exported as `standard | express`.
Orders placed without a priority behave as `standard`.
Invalid supplied priorities raise `OrderError`.
`reserveOrder` records `Backorder`s for shortages and keeps the order cancellable.
`listBackorders(state)` returns the recorded backorders.

children.title: Thread backorders through the service
children.objective: Expose the new domain operations through the application service and emit backorder events.
expectedOutcomes: The service exposes the backorder-aware operations from the domain.
Recording a backorder emits a warehouse event.
Service tests cover the new backorder path without changing unrelated behavior.

children.title: Prefer express work in a wave
children.objective: Keep the planner signature stable while ordering express orders before standard orders within one wave.
expectedOutcomes: `planFulfillment` preserves its existing signature.
Within a single wave, express orders are listed before standard orders.
Planner tests cover the new ordering without introducing unrelated behavior changes.

children.title: Count backorders in history analytics
children.objective: Derive a backorders count from journal events in HistoryAnalytics.
expectedOutcomes: `HistoryAnalytics` includes a backorders count.
The count is derived from recorded events rather than a separate source of truth.
Journal tests assert the new analytics field alongside existing behavior.

children.title: Expose backorders through the API
children.objective: Return the current state's backorders from the server surface.
expectedOutcomes: The server exposes the backorders of the current state.
The response shape stays compatible for existing callers except for the added backorders data.
API tests cover the new exposure path.

children.title: Differentiate order priority in SVG
children.objective: Render express orders distinctly from standard orders in the tower SVG.
expectedOutcomes: The rendered SVG makes express orders visually distinct from standard orders.
The existing tower rendering remains structurally intact outside the priority-specific styling or markers.
Presentation tests cover the distinction.

children.title: Add the g6 study probe
children.objective: Add a deterministic probe entrypoint and package script that emits one JSON object with byte-identical output across runs.
expectedOutcomes: `src/probe/g6.ts` exports `main()` returning a JSON string.
Direct invocation writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else.
Two invocations from the same commit produce byte-identical output.
The `study:g6-probe` script is added to the manifest and wired to the new probe.

- Order gains a readonly priority field of that type. It is optional at the call site: an order placed without a priority is treated as "standard", so existing callers keep working unchanged.
- placeOrder throws OrderError when a priority is supplied and is neither "standard" nor "express".
- Export interface Backorder with readonly orderId, skuId and missing fields, where missing is a positive integer.
- WarehouseState gains a readonly backorders field keyed by order id.
- reserveOrder records a Backorder for every line whose quantity exceeds the available units, instead of throwing, and leaves the order in a status from which it can still be cancelled.
- Export listBackorders(state) returning every recorded Backorder.

Application  - src/application/warehouse-service.ts:
- The service exposes the new operations and emits a warehouse event for a recorded backorder.

Fulfillment  - src/fulfillment/planner.ts:
- Within one wave, planFulfillment lists express orders before standard ones. Its existing signature does not change.

Durability  - src/durability/journal.ts:
- HistoryAnalytics gains a backorders count derived from the events.

API  - src/api/server.ts:
- The server exposes the backorders of the current state.

Presentation  - src/presentation/tower.ts:
- The rendered SVG distinguishes express orders from standard ones.

Probe  - src/probe/g6.ts and a package script named study:g6-probe:
- Follow the shape of the existing probes: export main() returning a JSON string, and write exactly one JSON object to stdout when invoked directly, with no other output.
- Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical output.
